title: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient as A Predictor of Liver SABR Treatment Outcome
official: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient as A Predictor of Liver SABR Treatment Outcome
summary: The ADAPTO study is a pilot trial where 6 participants receiving liver SABR treatment will be recruited. Participants will have MRI scans before treatment, then 1 week, 1 month, 3 months and 6 months after treatment, focusing partiuclarly on diffusion imaging (which creates a map of water movement over the imaging region). Since tumours are structured differently from healthy tissue, they look different on diffusion maps. Previous studies show that changes to the tumour caused by treatment should be visible on diffusion maps earlier after treatment than using the methods used at the moment to watch tumour response to treatment. This study will analyse the diffusion maps (both qualitatively and quantitatively) before and after treatment to investigate when tumour response can be detected and assessed using this imaging method compared with the standard follow up processes in use clinically. If tumour response can be accurately assessed at an earlier point than standard follow up processes when using diffusion imaging, this opens up possibilities to use this technique to reduce the time patients wait to know if their treatment has been effective and make clinical decision making possible at an earlier stage.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* older than 18 years old
* able to undergo MR scans for the duration for the study referred for liver SABR treatment
* able to provide informed consent and understand written and spoken English

Exclusion Criteria:

* they have a contraindication to 3T MRI, a gadolinium contrast allergy, or a recent GFR test indicating they are at risk of complications from being scanned using gadolinium contrast. Their status with respect to these factors will be monitored throughout the trial and they may receive additional GFR tests to ensure they can undergo contrast-enhanced MRI with minimal risk.
* they have an implant which is likely to reduce the quality of the images e.g. hip prosthesis. Certain implants, for example surgical/haemostatic clips, biopsy markers, stents, TIPS shunts and embolisation coils, could also present a risk of artefact for DWI at 3T and will be assessed at screening.
* they are pregnant (who will not be referred for SABR treatment and so would not reach the stage where participants are being selected).
